q: A transistor is a semiconductor device which works as an ____.
e: A transistor uses two junctions to control a large current with a small one. A transistor is a semiconductor device which works as an amplifier.

q: In ____, three American physicists Shockley, Bardeen and Brattain invented the transistor.
e: A transistor uses two junctions to control a large current with a small one. In 1949, three American physicists Shockley, Bardeen and Brattain invented the transistor.

q: A transistor is made of ____ layers of p- and n-semiconductors.
e: A transistor uses two junctions to control a large current with a small one. A transistor is made of three layers of p- and n-semiconductors.

q: There are two common kinds of transistors called the ____ transistors.
e: A transistor uses two junctions to control a large current with a small one. There are two common kinds of transistors called the pnp and npn transistors.

q: In a pnp transistor a thin layer of ____ is sandwiched between two layers of p-semiconductors.
e: A transistor uses two junctions to control a large current with a small one. In a pnp transistor a thin layer of n-semiconductor is sandwiched between two layers of p-semiconductors.

q: In an npn transistor a thin layer of ____ is sandwiched between two layers of n-semiconductors.
e: A transistor uses two junctions to control a large current with a small one. In an npn transistor a thin layer of p-semiconductor is sandwiched between two layers of n-semiconductors.

q: An electrode is attached to each layer and hence there are three electrodes; the ____, the collector (C) and the base (B) in a transistor.
e: A transistor uses two junctions to control a large current with a small one. An electrode is attached to each layer and hence there are three electrodes; the emitter(E), the collector (C) and the base (B) in a transistor.

q: Transistors do not ____ with time, whereas vacuum tubes do.
e: A transistor uses two junctions to control a large current with a small one. Transistors do not deteriorate with time, whereas vacuum tubes do.

q: Transistors are physically much more ____ than vacuum tubes.
e: A transistor uses two junctions to control a large current with a small one. Transistors are physically much more robust than vacuum tubes.

q: Transistors waste much less ____ than vacuum tubes.
e: A transistor uses two junctions to control a large current with a small one. Transistors waste much less electrical power than vacuum tubes.

q: There is no ____ after switching on a transistor.
e: A transistor uses two junctions to control a large current with a small one. There is no warm-up period after switching on a transistor.

q: Transistors are very much ____ than vacuum tubes but they perform a similar function.
e: A transistor uses two junctions to control a large current with a small one. Transistors are very much smaller than vacuum tubes but they perform a similar function.

q: In a transistor biasing circuit, a current ____ flows in the collector circuit.
e: A transistor uses two junctions to control a large current with a small one. In a transistor biasing circuit, a current I_C flows in the collector circuit.

q: The remainder of positive holes flows into the base so that the current ____ is obtained.
e: A missing valence electron is a positive hole. The hole behaves like a positive charge. The remainder of positive holes flows into the base so that the current I_B is obtained.

q: If $I_E$ is a current which flows across the emitter, then ____.
e: If I_E is a current which flows across the emitter, then I_E = I_C + I_B. Leave the relation as I_E = I_C + I_B.

q: However, the base is so thin that $I_B \sim 0.02 I_E$ and ____.
e: However, the base is so thin that I_B sim 0.02 I_E and I_C sim 0.98 I_E. I_c sim 0.98 i_e is what this statement is using.

q: Therefore, the small base current $I_B$ can control a very large ____.
e: Therefore, the small base current I_B can control a very large collector current. Collector current is what this statement is using.

q: Because of this property a transistor can be regarded as a ____.
e: A transistor uses two junctions to control a large current with a small one. Because of this property a transistor can be regarded as a current amplifier.

q: The resistance of forward-biased emitter junction is ____ and that of reverse-biased collector junction is large.
e: Resistance is V/I. A larger resistance gives a smaller current for the same voltage. The resistance of forward-biased emitter junction is small and that of reverse-biased collector junction is large.

q: Since the electrical power is ____, the power in the emitter side is small whereas the power in the collector side is large.
e: Work is F · s. Power is work per second, in watts. Since the electrical power is I²R, the power in the emitter side is small whereas the power in the collector side is large.

q: Therefore, the transistor can be regarded as a ____.
e: A transistor uses two junctions to control a large current with a small one. Therefore, the transistor can be regarded as a power amplifier.

q: Because the thickness of the base is about ____ and the base layer of a transistor is thinner than other two layers, the value of base current $I_B$ is very small.
e: A transistor uses two junctions to control a large current with a small one. Because the thickness of the base is about 10^-3 cm and the base layer of a transistor is thinner than other two layers, the value of base current I_B is very small.
